name: Glass Refraction
desc: The view through a pane of irregular glass — hand-blown crown rondels, fluted reeds, hammered dimples or a shattered sheet — each cell dragging the colour field behind it into a different place, fringing at the steep edges, with the lead came dark between and specular seams crawling as the pane drifts.

refraction.doc: displacement strength — flat plate to wildly warped

scale.doc: glass feature size — rondel diameter / reed pitch / shard size

density.doc: how much colour lies behind the pane

hue.doc: primary hue of the field behind the glass

style.doc: rondel: hand-blown crown-glass discs with pontil centres and spin rings, set in dark came · reeded: vertical flutes, everything smeared into columns · hammered: dense dimpled cell glass · shatter: rigid fractured shards, each displacing on its own, bright cracks between

act.doc: settle: the pane barely drifts · slide: strong parallax, the glass slides across the view · breathe: the refraction strength swells and slackens

seed.doc: deterministic seed — same number, same piece
